premises.text: Plastic waste is pervasive including microplastics, yet plastics enable modern products
premises.evidence_span: We're even finding microplastics in babies in the womb. This is insane. And so why are we producing so much of this stuff? It's because it's absolutely amazing

premises.text: Stabilized enzymes packaged inside plastics enable self-degradation after use
premises.evidence_span: commercializing a breakthrough technology that lets us stabilize enzymes and package them up inside of the plastics so they can self-degrade when we're done with them

premises.text: Coated enzymes act like scissors cutting polymer chains from the inside when triggered
premises.evidence_span: The enzymes act like scissors, cutting up the individual chains so that there's nothing left behind

premises.text: Triggering requires water and heat so degradation is on demand, not spontaneous
premises.evidence_span: degradation is on demand. It requires water and heat. It doesn't happen just on its own

premises.text: Drop-in additive uses small enzyme amounts and is readily scalable
premises.evidence_span: drop-in additive that's readily scalable. Enzymes are incredibly efficient, so we only need to use a little bit

premises.text: PLA beachhead ($3.5B, fast-growing) unlocks more compostable product types and favorable end-of-life conditions
premises.evidence_span: starting with PLA, which is the first compostable plastic. It's a $3.5 billion market, and it's one of the fastest growing segments within the industry

value.text: Make-and-break materials that degrade cleanly after use
value.evidence_span: changing the way that we make and break materials so that we can live more harmoniously with nature

causal_links.evidence_span: self-degrade when we're done with them
enable a wider variety of favorable conditions at the end of life

notes: Warm-water infrastructure merged into the triggered-degradation story rather than a separate ops premise in this run. Team credentials excluded.
